_what_this_is: A record of which api/ routes were OBSERVED INVOKED in production over a real window. Read by tools/sairn_reachability_check.py --activity. It is an observation with a date on it, not a standing fact: re-capture before trusting it, exactly like tools/sairn_dom_snapshot.js output.
_how_to_recapture: Vercel MCP: get_runtime_logs(projectId, teamId, environment='production', since='72h', group_by='requestPath'). 24h and 72h both return; 7d TIMED OUT and 30d returned 400 on 2026-09-13, so 72h is the practical ceiling and the window is SHORT. Paste the table into counts below, set captured_at and window_hours, and leave everything else derived.
_why_it_is_a_file_and_not_a_network_call: Every checker in tools/ is offline and read-only, and the reachability checker's existing --live flag already takes a captured DOM snapshot for the same reason. A checker that reaches the network cannot run in a hook, a cron, or on a plane, and it fails in a way that looks like a clean pass.
source: Vercel runtime logs, production, grouped by requestPath
_cron_paths_are_DERIVED: The checker reads vercel.json's own crons array rather than trusting a list here. On 2026-09-13 that is /api/sairndental/send-reminder and /api/alf-alerts, both hourly, which is exactly the 72 each over 72 hours.
_unattributed_is_named_rather_than_guess: Everything that is not a declared cron is UNATTRIBUTED, not 'organic'. This platform has no request-level attribution, so a hit cannot be separated into customer traffic, a session's own live-verification fetch, a deploy check, or an uptime probe. /api/sd-data's 71 over 72 hours is the clearest case: it is almost exactly hourly and NOTHING EXPLAINS IT. The obvious guess was that a cron calls it -- grep found 'sd-data' in api/sairndental/send-reminder.js and the hit was a COMMENT saying that file BYPASSES sd-data. That is PR 1.2 one more time, in the analysis rather than in a tool, and it is why this field says unattributed instead of inventing a bucket.
